questions.question: Change the narration: Kiran asked me, "Did you see the Cricket match on television last night?"

options.a: Kiran asked me whether I saw the Cricket match on television the earlier night.
options.b: Kiran asked me whether I had seen the Cricket match on television the earlier night.
options.c: Kiran asked me did I see the Cricket match on television the last night.
options.d: Kiran asked me whether I had seen the Cricket match on television the last night.

questions.correct_answer_text: Kiran asked me whether I had seen the Cricket match on television the earlier night.
questions.explanation: "Did you see" (Simple Past) → "whether I had seen" (Past Perfect). "Last night" → "the earlier night/the previous night".

questions.question: Change the narration: He said to interviewer, "Could you please repeat the question?"

options.a: He requested the interviewer if he could please repeat the question.
options.b: He requested the interviewer to please repeat the question.
options.c: He requested the interviewer to repeat the question.
options.d: He requested the interviewer if he could repeat the question.

questions.correct_answer_text: He requested the interviewer to repeat the question.
questions.explanation: Polite request "Could you please…" → "requested + object + to + base verb". "Please" is dropped.

questions.question: Change the narration: The government has announced, "Taxes will be raised":

options.a: The government has announced that taxes would be raised.
options.b: The government has announced that taxes would raised.
options.c: The government has announced that taxes will be raised.
options.d: The government has announced taxes will be raised.

questions.correct_answer_text: The government has announced that taxes will be raised.
questions.explanation: Reporting verb is Present Tense ("has announced") → tense of reported speech does NOT change. "will be raised" stays as is.

questions.question: Change the narration: I told him that he was not working hard.

options.a: I said to him, "You are not working hard."
options.b: I told to him, "You are not working hard."
options.c: I said, "You are not working hard."
options.d: I said to him, "He is not working hard."

questions.correct_answer_text: I said to him, "You are not working hard."
questions.explanation: Indirect → Direct: "told him that he was not working hard" → "said to him, 'You are not working hard.'" Pronoun "he" → "you".

questions.question: Change the narration: The doctor says, "It is better you undergo a surgery next week."

options.a: The doctor advised me to undergo a surgery the following week.
options.b: The doctor says that it is better I undergo a surgery the following week.
options.c: The doctor says that it was better I underwent a surgery the coming week.
options.d: The doctor advises that it is better I underwent a surgery the following week.

questions.correct_answer_text: The doctor says that it is better I undergo a surgery the following week.
questions.explanation: Reporting verb "says" is Present → tense unchanged. "Next week" → "the following week".

questions.question: Change the narration: Sachin said, "My grandfather recites the Geeta every morning."

options.a: Sachin told that his grandfather has cited the Geeta every morning.
options.b: Sachin told that his grandfather recited the Geeta every morning.
options.c: Sachin said that his grandfather recites the Geeta every morning.
options.d: Sachin said that his grandfather recited the Geeta every morning.

questions.correct_answer_text: Sachin said that his grandfather recites the Geeta every morning.
questions.explanation: Universal/habitual truth → tense remains unchanged in indirect speech. "recites the Geeta every morning" stays unchanged.

questions.question: Change the narration: Suma said to him, "Am I to wait for you forever?"

options.a: Suma asked him if she were to wait for him forever.
options.b: Suma said to him if she can wait for him forever.
options.c: Suma asked him if she was to wait for him forever.
options.d: Suma asked him if she had to wait for him forever.

questions.correct_answer_text: Suma asked him if she was to wait for him forever.
questions.explanation: "Am I to wait" → "if she was to wait". Pronoun "I" → "she", "you" → "him".

questions.question: Change the narration: "Don't pull the dog's tail," his father said.

options.a: His father said that he did not pull the dog's tail.
options.b: His father forbade him not to pull the dog's tail.
options.c: His father told him to pull the dog's tail.
options.d: His father told him not to pull the dog's tail.

questions.correct_answer_text: His father told him not to pull the dog's tail.
questions.explanation: Negative imperative "Don't + verb" → "told + object + not to + base verb".

questions.question: Change the narration: "And you believe all this?" asked Sriram, in surprise.

options.a: Sriram asked me in surprise if I believed all this.
options.b: Sriram asked me in disbelief if I was believing all this.
options.c: Surprised, Sriram asked me whether I believed all that.
options.d: Sriram was amazed that I believed all that.

questions.correct_answer_text: Surprised, Sriram asked me whether I believed all that.
questions.explanation: "In surprise" → participle "Surprised". "this" → "that". "Believe" → "believed".

questions.question: Change the narration: She yelled, "Please help me."

options.a: She yelled at one for some help.
options.b: She yelled for someone to help.
options.c: She yelled for someone to help her.
options.d: She yelled at someone to help her.

questions.correct_answer_text: She yelled for someone to help her.
questions.explanation: Earnest plea "Please help me" → "yelled for someone to help her". "me" → "her".

questions.question: Change the narration: He said, "If I had the key with me, I could give you the solution".

options.a: He said that if he had the key with him, he could give him/her the solution.
options.b: He said if he could have the key with him, he would give him/her the solution.
options.c: He told that if he could have the key with him, he would give him/her the solution.
options.d: He said that if he have had the key with him, he could have given him/her the solution.

questions.correct_answer_text: He said that if he had the key with him, he could give him/her the solution.
questions.explanation: Type 2 conditional: structure remains the same. Pronouns change: "I" → "he", "me" → "him", "you" → "him/her".

questions.question: Change the narration: The poor examinee said, "O God, take pity on me."

options.a: The poor examinee prayed God to take pity on him.
options.b: The poor examinee, invoking God, implored him to take pity on him.
options.c: The poor examinee exclaimed that God take pity on him.
options.d: The poor examinee asked God to take pity on him.

questions.correct_answer_text: The poor examinee, invoking God, implored him to take pity on him.
questions.explanation: "O God" = invocation → "invoking God". The earnest plea "take pity on me" → "implored him to take pity on him".

questions.question: Change the narration: Gavaskar said, "Bravo! Azhar, you have done well."

options.a: Gavaskar exclaimed with joy that Azhar had done well.
options.b: Gavaskar called Azhar and exclaimed that he had done well.
options.c: Gavaskar congratulated Azhar, saying that he had done well.
options.d: Gavaskar praised Azhar for his having done well.

questions.correct_answer_text: Gavaskar congratulated Azhar, saying that he had done well.
questions.explanation: "Bravo!" addressed to a person = congratulation → "congratulated Azhar, saying that he had done well". "have done" → "had done".

questions.question: Change the narration: Mary said to Robert, "Let him come, then we shall see."

options.a: Mary said to Robert that if he came, they would see him.
options.b: Mary told Robert that they shall see him if he came.
options.c: Mary told Robert that once he came, they would see him.
options.d: Mary told Robert that they would see him if he might come.

questions.correct_answer_text: Mary told Robert that they would see him if he might come.
questions.explanation: Conditional suggestion → "told Robert that they would see him if he might come". "shall" → "would", "let him come" → "if he might come".

questions.question: Change the narration: The spectators said, "Bravo! well played, Ravi."

options.a: The spectators called Ravi bravo because he had played well.
options.b: The spectators said that Ravi played well and applauded him.
options.c: The spectators encouraged Ravi saying that he played well.
options.d: The spectators applauded Ravi, saying that he had played well.

questions.correct_answer_text: The spectators applauded Ravi, saying that he had played well.
questions.explanation: "Bravo! well played" = applause/praise → "applauded Ravi, saying that he had played well". "played" → "had played".

questions.question: Change the narration: He said, "The mice will play, when the cat is away."

options.a: He said that the mice will play when the cat is away.
options.b: He said that the mice would play when the cat was away.
options.c: He said that the mice would play when the cat would be away.
options.d: He said that the mice shall play, when the cat is away.

questions.correct_answer_text: He said that the mice would play when the cat was away.
questions.explanation: Reporting verb "said" is past → "will play" → "would play", "is away" → "was away".

questions.question: Change the narration: Rajan said, "O that I were a child again!"

options.a: Rajan exclaimed with wonder that he was a child again.
options.b: Rajan wondered that were he a child again.
options.c: Rajan strongly wished that he had been a child again.
options.d: Rajan prayed that he were a child again.

questions.correct_answer_text: Rajan strongly wished that he had been a child again.
questions.explanation: "O that I were…!" = strong wish → "strongly wished that he had been a child again". Subjunctive "were" → past perfect "had been".

questions.question: Change the narration: He said to her, "Don't read so fast."

options.a: He told her not to read so fast.
options.b: He advised her don't read so fast.
options.c: He requested her not to read so fast.
options.d: He ordered her not to read so fast.

questions.correct_answer_text: He told her not to read so fast.
questions.explanation: Negative imperative → "told + object + not to + base verb".

questions.question: Change the narration: The Manager said, "Well, what can I do for you?"

options.a: The Manager asked what he could do for him.
options.b: The Manager wondered what he could do for him.
options.c: The Manager wanted to know what he could do for him.
options.d: The Manager said that he couldn't do anything for him.

questions.correct_answer_text: The Manager wanted to know what he could do for him.
questions.explanation: Polite enquiry → "wanted to know what he could do for him". "Well" dropped. "can" → "could".

questions.question: Change the narration: "Are we never to meet?" Amit asked him.

options.a: Amit questioned him whether they were ever to be meet.
options.b: Amit wondered whether they are never to meet.
options.c: Amit said whether they were never to meet.
options.d: Amit asked him whether they were never to meet.

questions.correct_answer_text: Amit asked him whether they were never to meet.
questions.explanation: Yes/No question → "asked him whether…". "Are" → "were", "we" → "they".

questions.question: Change the narration: I said to the boy, "You have no ticket, get out before you are driven out."

options.a: I told the boy get out before you are driven out.
options.b: I told the boy to get out before he was driven out as he had no ticket.
options.c: I ordered the boy to get out before he was driven out.
options.d: I told the boy that he had no ticket and that he should get out before he was driven out.

questions.correct_answer_text: I told the boy to get out before he was driven out as he had no ticket.
questions.explanation: Combined statement + command. "told the boy to get out before he was driven out as he had no ticket." Reason embedded using "as".

questions.question: Change the narration: Sachin said, "My grandfather recites the Geeta every morning." (Repeat for practice)

options.a: Sachin told that his grandfather has cited the Geeta every morning.
options.b: Sachin told that his grandfather recited the Geeta every morning.
options.c: Sachin said that his grandfather recites the Geeta every morning.
options.d: Sachin said that his grandfather recited the Geeta every morning.

questions.correct_answer_text: Sachin said that his grandfather recites the Geeta every morning.
questions.explanation: Habitual truth → tense unchanged in indirect speech.
